boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the ten frozen records without dossiers in Grant's Operations Against Vicksburg [March-July 1863]; the existing MS009 draft is unchanged. Preserve per-engagement dates. MS011's frozen siege interval (May 18–July 4) contains the separate Milliken's Bend (June 7), Goodrich's Landing (June 29–30) and Helena (July 4) engagements; campaign-wide loss figures must not be assigned to any one engagement. Opening personnel and exact effective command boundaries remain unresolved. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. The frozen side-specific numerical strength bounds are blank (missing_numeric_strength). No figure in this pass is adopted as a simultaneous opening force.

claims.value: The frozen force field names the Army of the Tennessee (two corps) and one reinforced Confederate division of four brigades, without counts; the live field reads zero. Greene says Bowen's force numbered about 8,500 by the latest returns, that Bowen gave 5,500 in his official report, and that the Union force engaged was 23,000. Bowen's postscript to his May 2 synopsis says the enemy exceeded 20,000 and his own force did not number over 5,500; on the day he telegraphed that they outnumbered him trebly.
claims.rationale: Returns, report and opponent figures differ in scope and source; none is adopted as matched opening strength. Greene dates the 5,500 to a report three months later, while the inspected May 2 postscript also gives it. Live zeros are not measured absence.

claims.value: Greene says McClernand repeatedly asked for reinforcements although he had three divisions against about a brigade and a half, and that Grant sent McPherson to turn the Confederate right. Bowen says he attempted with two of Cockrell's regiments to turn the Union right, that Tracy was killed early, and that Baldwin, misled by the burning of the railroad bridge, took the wrong road and destroyed the north-fork bridge. The live heading ranks Grant Lieutenant General against the frozen Major General.
claims.rationale: Subordinate and corps roles from a history and an interested report; the frozen commanders Grant and Bowen do not receive automatic sole credit. The heading rank is not adopted.

claims.value: The frozen casualty text reads 1,648 total (US 861; CS 787); the live field reads 1662 total (US 875; CS 787;). Greene gives Bowen's reported losses as 787 (60 killed, 340 wounded, 387 missing) and Grant's as 849, and says Union reports put Confederate prisoners at over 600. Bowen's synopsis gives no estimate.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap. Three Union totals (861, 875, 849) differ; the Confederate 787 agrees across frozen, live and Greene.

open_questions: Bowen's detailed June 4 report, the brigade reports, McClernand's and Grant's reports and the compiled returns remain deferred; Pemberton's May 1 telegram giving Bowen about 9,000 is outside the selected Bowen text.

NPS/CWSAC is one family. Greene is one retrospective history by a non-participant, founded on the Official Records. Each report author selected from Official Records Volumes XXIV and XXII is a separate family of interested accounts; the volumes are shared containers, not additional witnesses, and letters or telegrams by others quoted inside a selected document are not separate families. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
